scope: A INSERT statement driver over the C0 Row write boundary through private traits. insert_statement runs rows and finishes a fully applied statement; a statement with applied rows is handed back RollbackRequired inside PendingRollback<S>, whose private fields allow only start_statement_rollback (start_full_rollback for a transaction from a conflicting commit), release by rolled_back() after the rollback started from it finished, or drop into C's fence; the rollback is caller-driven (start -> rollback_step... -> finish_rollback -> rolled_back -> finish_statement/finish_aborted). Runtime cases use test-only literal stand-ins (call log, row high-water, actor chain, statement mark, scripted refusals); A's pure encode_input runs in the validation stand-in; expected bytes/digests/frame lengths are independent literals from make_driver_literals.py. Live entries are compile-checked only (gap G2).

review_fixes.ADV1: statement atomicity in the type: After::RollbackRequired carries PendingRollback<H> (private handle + progress Required/Started/Finished); start_statement_rollback/start_full_rollback take &mut PendingRollback and return StartedRollback<'r, K>, whose successful finish alone marks it Finished; rolled_back() yields the handle only then; a second start is refused without a C call (OrderMismatch; must-resolve after an abandoned or fenced start). A compile-fail probe is impractical for crate-private items, so the guarantee is documented on the type and D14 tests every reachable path.
review_fixes.ADV2: finish_aborted: C's RollbackRequired after a finished full rollback maps to MustResolve(Some(transaction)) with must_resolve, never After::RollbackRequired (no second full RollbackStart); documented under G5; D13 asserts it.
